source.title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages

accepted.question_text: Let (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) be a probability-measure-preserving system with commuting transformations, and let f0, f1, ..., fℓ be bounded measurable functions. Define the multiple correlation sequence C: Z^ℓ → C by C(n1, ..., nℓ) = ∫ f0 · T1^n1 f1 · ... · Tℓ^nℓ fℓ dμ. Is every such sequence an exact or approximate integral combination of generalized ℓ-step nilsequences in ℓ variables?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Determine the structure of the multiple correlation sequences (C(n1, . . . , n`)) defined by (14). Is it true that any such sequence is an (approximate) integral combination of generalized `-step nilsequences in `-variables?

accepted.question_text: Let C_{T,S} be the set of sequences of the form a(n) = ∫ f · T^n g · S^n h dμ, where (X, X, μ, T, S) ranges over all measure-preserving systems and f, g, h are bounded measurable functions, and let C_T be the subclass obtained when T and S are powers of a single transformation. Are these two classes equal, i.e. does every sequence arising from two commuting transformations already arise from powers of one transformation?

evidence.quote: Problem 2. Show that CT,S = CT .

accepted.question_text: For integer sequences a1(n), ..., aℓ(n), prove that the following are equivalent: (i) for every probability-measure-preserving system with commuting transformations T1, ..., Tℓ and every bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{a1(n)} f1 · ... · Tℓ^{aℓ(n)} fℓ converge in L^2; (ii) the same convergence holds for all ℓ-step nilsystems; and (iii) for every basic generalized ℓ-step nilsequence ψ in ℓ variables, the scalar averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N ψ(a1(n), ..., aℓ(n)) converge.

evidence.quote: Problem 3. If (a1(n)), . . . ,(a`(n)) are sequences of integers, then show that the following statements are equivalent: • The sequences (a1(n)), . . . ,(a`(n)) are good for `-convergence of commuting transformations. • The sequences (a1(n)), . . . ,(a`(n)) are good for `-convergence of `-step nilsystems. • The sequence (1/N)PN n=1 ψ(a1(n), . . . , a`(n)) converges for every basic generalized `-step nilsequence ψ in `-variables.

accepted.question_text: Let a(n) be an integer sequence such that, for every connected ℓ-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b on X, the orbit b^{a(n)}Γ is equidistributed in X, and such that for every positive integer r the set {n ∈ N : r divides a(n)} has positive upper density. Must a(n) then be good for ℓ-recurrence of commuting transformations, meaning that for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, there exists n with μ(A ∩ T1^{a(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{a(n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Let (a(n)) be a sequence that satisfies: • for every connected `-step nilmanifold X and every irrational nilrotation b in X the sequence (b^{a(n)}Γ)n∈N is equidistributed in X, and • the set {n ∈ N: r|a(n)} has positive upper density for every r ∈ N. Show that the sequence (a(n)) is good for `-recurrence of commuting transformations.

accepted.question_text: Suppose an integer sequence a(n) is good for ℓ-recurrence of powers, meaning that for every nonzero integers k1, ..., kℓ and every measure-preserving transformation T, some n gives positive measure to A ∩ T^{k1 a(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ T^{kℓ a(n)}A whenever μ(A) > 0. Does it follow that each power sequence a(n)^k is good for ordinary 1-recurrence for every k = 1, ..., ℓ?
accepted.context_brief: Recurrence of powers of recurrent sequences

evidence.quote: Problem 5. If (a(n)) is good for `-recurrence of powers, is then (a(n)^k) good for 1-recurrence for k = 1, . . . , `?

accepted.question_text: If an integer sequence a(n) is good for 2-convergence of powers of a single transformation, does it automatically remain good for 2-convergence of two arbitrary commuting transformations?
accepted.context_brief: Two-fold convergence: powers versus commuting maps

evidence.quote: Problem 6. If a sequence is good for 2-convergence of powers, then show that it is good for 2-convergence of commuting transformations.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist an integer sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but fails to be good for 2-recurrence of arbitrary commuting transformations?
accepted.context_brief: Two-fold recurrence: powers versus commuting maps

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Is there a sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?

accepted.question_text: Find an explicit fast-growing integer sequence a(n), meaning log a(n) / log n → ∞, that is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence both for powers of a single transformation and for arbitrary commuting transformations.

evidence.quote: Problem 8. Give an explicit example of a fast growing sequence that is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers and commuting transformations.

accepted.question_text: Let P = {p1, ..., pℓ} be a family of essentially distinct integer polynomials, and let d_min(P) be the smallest integer d such that the Host-Kra factor Z_d is characteristic for mean convergence of the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · T^{pℓ(n)}fℓ for every system. Is d_min(P) always at most |P| - 1 whenever |P| ≥ 2?

evidence.quote: Problem 9. If |P| ≥ 2, show that dmin(P) ≤ |P| − 1.

accepted.question_text: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials in the sense defined in the paper. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable functions f1, ..., fℓ, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[p1,N(n)]}f1 · ... · T^{[pℓ,N(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2 to (∫ f1 dμ) · ... · (∫ fℓ dμ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Suppose that the sequence of `-tuples of polynomials (p1,N , . . . , p`,N ) is good. Show that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and functions f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ) we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^[p1,N (n)]f1 · · · T^[p`,N (n)]f` = ∫ f1 dµ · · · ∫ f` dµ where convergence takes place in L^2(µ).

accepted.question_text: For every probability-measure-preserving system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable functions f, g, h, do the multiple ergodic averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) h(T^{3n} x) and (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(T^{n^2} x) converge for μ-almost every x?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Let (X, X , µ, T) be a system and f, g, h ∈ L∞(µ) be functions. Show that the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 f(T^n x) · g(T^2n x) · h(T^3n x) and the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 f(T^n x) · g(T^n^2 x) converge pointwise almost everywhere.

accepted.question_text: Let T be a measure-preserving transformation, f and g bounded measurable, Λ the von Mangoldt function, and φ a multiplicative function taking values in the unit disk and having convergent means on every arithmetic progression. Do the weighted double averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N Λ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) and (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N φ(n) f(T^n x) g(T^{2n} x) converge for almost every x?
accepted.context_brief: Arithmetic weights in pointwise ergodic averages

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Let (X, X , µ, T) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ) be functions. If Λ is the von Mangoldt function and φ is a multiplicative function that takes values on the complex unit disc and has convergent means, then show that the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 Λ(n) f(T^n x) · g(T^2n x) and the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 φ(n) f(T^n x) · g(T^2n x) converge pointwise almost everywhere.

accepted.question_text: Let a(n) be one of the sequences of prime numbers p_n, the Hardy-type sequence [n^c] with c > 0, or the exponential sequence 2^n. For every ergodic system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable f0, ..., fℓ, does the multiple correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T^{a(n)}f1 · ... · T^{ℓ a(n)}fℓ dμ always admit a decomposition ψ(a(n)) + e(n), where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro mean of |e(n)| tends to 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Let (a(n)) be the sequence of integers (pn), where pn is the n-th prime, or ([n^c]), where c > 0, or (2^n). Is it true that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and all functions f0, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ), one has a decomposition ∫ f0 · T^a(n)f1 · . . . · T^`a(n)f` dµ = ψ(a(n)) + e(n), where (ψ(n)) is an (`-step) nilsequence and limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 |e(n)| = 0?

accepted.question_text: If p1, ..., pℓ are integer-valued generalized polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ always converge in L^2?

evidence.quote: Problem 14. Let p1, . . . , p` be integer valued generalized polynomials. Show that the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^p1(n) f1 · · · T`^p`(n) f` converge in the mean as N → ∞.

accepted.question_text: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are pairwise independent integer polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. Does there exist d such that the Host-Kra factors Z_{d,T1}, ..., Z_{d,Tℓ} are characteristic for the polynomial averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ?
accepted.context_brief: Characteristic factors for commuting polynomial averages

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Suppose that the polynomials p1, . . . , p` ∈ Z[t] are pairwise independent. Show that there exists d ∈ N such that the factors Zd,T1, . . . , Zd,T` are characteristic factors for the averages (17).

accepted.question_text: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are rationally independent integer polynomials and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. Are the rational Kronecker factors Krat(T1), ..., Krat(Tℓ) characteristic for the polynomial averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{p1(n)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}fℓ?
accepted.context_brief: Rational Kronecker factors for commuting polynomials

evidence.quote: Problem 16. Suppose that the polynomials p1, . . . , p` ∈ Z[t] are rationally independent. Show that Krat(T1), . . . , Krat(T`) are characteristic factors for the averages (17).

accepted.question_text: Suppose p1, ..., pℓ are rationally independent integer polynomials with zero constant term and T1, ..., Tℓ are commuting measure-preserving transformations. For every measurable set A of positive measure and every ε > 0, must there exist n with μ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}A) at least μ(A)^{ℓ+1} - ε?
accepted.context_brief: Optimal lower bounds for polynomial recurrence

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Suppose that the polynomials p1, . . . , p` ∈ Z[t] are rationally independent and have zero constant term. Show that for every A ∈ X and every ε > 0, there exists n ∈ N such that µ(A ∩ T1^p1(n)A ∩ · · · ∩ T`^p`(n)A) ≥ µ(A)^`+1 − ε.

accepted.question_text: Let p1, ..., pℓ be an intersective family of integer polynomials, meaning that for every positive integer r there exists n with p_i(n) divisible by r for all i. For every commuting measure-preserving system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, must there exist n such that μ(A ∩ T1^{p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{pℓ(n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 18. Let (X, X , µ, T1, . . . , T`) be a system and {p1, . . . , p`} be a family of intersective integer polynomials. Show that for every set A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0 one has µ(A ∩ T1^p1(n)A ∩ · · · ∩ T`^p`(n)A) > 0 for some n ∈ N.

accepted.question_text: For every system with two commuting measure-preserving transformations T and S and bounded measurable functions f and g, do the bilinear averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^n x) g(S^n x) converge for almost every x?

evidence.quote: Problem 19. Let (X, X , µ, T, S) be a system and f, g ∈ L∞(µ) be functions. Show that the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 f(T^n x) · g(S^n x) converge pointwise almost everywhere.

accepted.question_text: For commuting measure-preserving transformations T1, ..., Tℓ and bounded measurable f0, ..., fℓ, does every correlation sequence ∫ f0 · T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ dμ admit a decomposition ψ(n) + e(n), where ψ is an ℓ-step nilsequence and the Cesàro mean of |e(n)| tends to 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 20. Is it true that one always has a decomposition ∫ f0 · T1^n f1 · . . . · T`^n f` dµ = ψ(n) + e(n) where (ψ(n)) is an `-step nilsequence and limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 |e(n)| = 0?

accepted.question_text: Let T1, ..., Tℓ be arbitrary invertible measure-preserving transformations, not assumed to commute, and let p1, ..., pℓ be distinct integer polynomials with zero constant term. For every measurable set A with positive measure, must there exist m, n ∈ N such that μ(A ∩ T1^{m+p1(n)}A ∩ ... ∩ Tℓ^{m+pℓ(n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Let (X, X , µ) be a probability space, T1, . . . , T` : X → X be invertible measure preserving transformations, and p1, . . . , p` be distinct polynomials with zero constant term. Show that for every A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0 we have µ(A ∩ T1^(m+p1(n))A ∩ · · · ∩ T`^(m+p`(n))A) > 0 for some m, n ∈ N.

accepted.question_text: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth. Is the family of integer-part sequences {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} good for ℓ-fold mean convergence for a single transformation exactly when every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) satisfies one of the three asymptotic alternatives stated in the paper: either |a(t) - c p(t)| / log t → ∞ for every real c and integer polynomial p, or a(t) - c p(t) → d for some real c, d, or |a(t) - t/m| ≤ C log t for some nonzero integer m and constant C?

evidence.quote: Problem 22. Let F be as above. Show that the family of sequences {([a1(n)]), . . . , ([a`(n)])} is good for `-convergence of a single transformation if and only if every function a ∈ span∗(F) satisfies one of the following conditions: • |a(t) − cp(t)|/ log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]; or • a(t) − cp(t) → d for some c, d ∈ R; or • |a(t) − t/m| ≤ C log t for some non-zero m ∈ Z and C > 0.

accepted.question_text: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays farther than O(log t) from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. For every ergodic system (X, B, μ, T) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, must the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[a1(n)]}f1 · ... · T^{[aℓ(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2 to (∫ f1 dμ) · ... · (∫ fℓ dμ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 23. Let F be as above and suppose that for every function a ∈ span∗(F) we have |a(t) − cp(t)|/ log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]. Show that for every ergodic system (X, B, µ, T) and functions f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ) we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^[a1(n)]f1 · · · T^[a`(n)]f` = ∫ f1 dµ · · · ∫ f` dµ where the convergence takes place in L^2(µ).

accepted.question_text: If a and b are distinct positive non-integers, then for every ergodic system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable functions f and g, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^{[n^a]}x) g(T^{[n^b]}x) converge almost everywhere to (∫ f dμ)(∫ g dμ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let a, b be distinct positive non-integers. Show that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and functions f, g ∈ L∞(µ), we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 f(T^[n^a]x) · g(T^[n^b]x) = ∫ f dµ · ∫ g dµ for almost every x ∈ X.

accepted.question_text: Let F = {a1, ..., aℓ} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth such that every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) stays unboundedly far from every real multiple of every integer polynomial. Must the integer-part family {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} then be good for ℓ-recurrence for a single transformation?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Let F be as above and suppose that for every function a ∈ span∗(F) we have |a(t) − cp(t)| → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]. Show that the collection of sequences {([a1(n)]), . . . ,([a`(n)])} is good for `-recurrence of a single transformation.

accepted.question_text: Find a Hardy-field function a(t) with super-polynomial growth, meaning a(t) / t^k → ∞ for every k, such that the integer sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation.

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Find an example of a function a ∈ H that grows faster than polynomials, meaning, a(t)/t^k → ∞ for every k ∈ N, such that the sequence [a(n)] is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

accepted.question_text: If c is a positive non-integer and p_n denotes the n-th prime, is the sequence [p_n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation?

evidence.quote: Problem 27. Let c be a positive non-integer. Show that the sequence ([p_n^c]) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

accepted.question_text: Is the oscillatory integer sequence [n sin n] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence of powers of a single transformation?

evidence.quote: Problem 28. Show that the sequence ([n sin n]) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of powers.

accepted.question_text: If c > 1 is nonintegral, is the integer sequence [n^c] good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence for arbitrary commuting transformations? More specifically, for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, does the L^2-limit of (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{[n^c]}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{[n^c]}fℓ exist and equal the L^2-limit of the linear averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^n f1 · ... · Tℓ^n fℓ?

evidence.quote: Problem 29. Show that if c > 1 is not an integer, then the sequence ([n^c]) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of commuting transformations. Moreover, show that if (X, X , µ, T1, . . . , T`) is a system and f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ), then the L^2(µ)-limit limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^[n^c]f1 · · · T`^[n^c]f` is equal to the L^2(µ)-limit limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^n f1 · · · T`^n f`.

accepted.question_text: Let c, c1, ..., cℓ be positive real numbers. Do the prime numbers contain infinitely many configurations of the form {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], ..., m + ℓ[n^c]} and, more generally, {m, m + [n^{c1}], ..., m + [n^{cℓ}]}?

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Let ` ∈ N and c, c1, . . . , c` be positive real numbers. Show that the prime numbers contain patterns of the form {m, m + [n^c], m + 2[n^c], . . . , m + `[n^c]} and {m, m + [n^c1], . . . , m + [n^c`]} for infinitely many n ∈ N.

accepted.question_text: Consider the random increasing sequence a_n(ω) obtained by selecting each integer n independently with probability σ_n, where nσ_n → ∞. Almost surely, is this random sequence good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence for commuting transformations? Equivalently, for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, do the random averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{a_n(ω)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{a_n(ω)}fℓ converge in L^2 to the same limit as the deterministic averages along n?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Suppose that nσn → ∞. Show that almost surely the sequence (an(ω)) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of commuting transformations. Moreover, show that almost surely the following holds: For every system (X, X , µ, T1, . . . , T`) and functions f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^an(ω) f1 · · · T`^an(ω) f` converge in L^2(µ) and their limit equals the limit of the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^n f1 · · · T`^n f`.

accepted.question_text: Let a_n(ω) be a random increasing sequence generated by independent selectors with nσ_n → ∞. Almost surely, for every system (X, X, μ, T, S) and bounded measurable f and g, do the mixed averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^n f · S^{a_n(ω)} g converge in L^2 to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)? If in addition σ_n = n^{-a} for some a in (0, 1), does almost sure pointwise convergence also hold?

evidence.quote: Problem 32. Suppose that nσn → ∞. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system (X, X , µ, T, S) and functions f, g ∈ L∞(µ), we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^n f · S^an(ω) g = E(f|IT) · E(g|IS) where the limit is taken in L^2(µ). Furthermore, if σn = n^−a for some a ∈ (0, 1), show that the convergence also holds pointwise almost everywhere.

accepted.question_text: Let a_n(ω) and b_n(ω) be two independent random increasing sequences built from selector probabilities n^{-a} and n^{-b} with a, b in (0, 1) and a ≠ b. Almost surely, for every system (X, X, μ, T, S) and bounded measurable f and g, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{a_n(ω)} f · S^{b_n(ω)} g converge, in L^2 or pointwise, to E(f | I_T) · E(g | I_S)?

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Suppose that a, b ∈ (0, 1) and a 6= b. Show that almost surely the following holds: For every system (X, X , µ, T, S) and functions f, g ∈ L∞(µ) we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^an(ω) f · S^bn(ω) g = E(f|IT) · E(g|IS) where the limit is taken in L^2(µ) or pointwise.

accepted.question_text: Let (X, X, μ, T_n) be a measure-preserving system with multiplicative structure, meaning T_0 = T_1 = id and T_m ∘ T_n = T_{mn}. For every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, must there exist integers m > n ≥ 1 such that μ(T_{2mn}A ∩ T_{(m-n)(m+n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 34. Let (X, X , µ, Tn) be a measure preserving system with multiplicative structure and A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0. Is it true that there exist m, n ∈ N, m > n, such that µ(T2mnA ∩ T(m−n)(m+n)A) > 0 ?

accepted.question_text: Let (X, X, μ, T_n) be a measure-preserving system with multiplicative structure, meaning T_m ∘ T_n = T_{mn}. For every measurable A with μ(A) > 0, must there exist m, n ∈ N such that μ(T_{m(m+n)}A ∩ T_{(m+2n)(m+3n)}A ∩ T_{(m+4n)(m+5n)}A) > 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 35. Let (X, X , µ, Tn) be a measure preserving system with multiplicative structure and A ∈ X with µ(A) > 0. Is it true that there exist m, n ∈ N such that µ(Tm(m+n)A ∩ T(m+2n)(m+3n) ∩ T(m+4n)(m+5n)A) > 0 ?
